checks.text: Is every entity in an ABE folder under its home capability, with one Primary Entity per ABE (named after its folder), and is every entity name unique (`mde verify`, Entity placement row)?
Is every rule of its own file linked from an entity it governs, and every rule id used once (`mde verify`, Business rules row)?
Does each capability's overview list the ABEs it uses, its own first, and link each of its workflows (`mde verify`, Capabilities row)?
Are the Domain's Purpose and Scope written, not left as "Not yet described" (`mde verify`, Domain row)?
Does every link inside the requirements resolve (`mde verify`, Requirement links row)?

Does every entity have an attributes table with types of the Method and a key, a Display label naming its attributes (not the bare id), its relationships as the table (Related, Role, Cardinality, Kind, Cascade) with valid values linking real entities, transitions only between its declared states, and an enum attribute holding those states (`mde verify`, Entity model row)?
Is every operation that changes something invoked by some use case (`mde verify`, Operations used row)?
Are roles kept only at the top level (`specs/requirements/roles/`), each the actor of some use case (`mde verify`, Roles row)?
Does every use case name roles that exist as its actors, and invoke only operations its entities declare (`mde verify`, Use case references row)?

Does every import resolve to a declared dependency (`mde verify`, Imports declared row)?

checks.text: Is code coverage instrumented for real, with the instrumented runs named, the matrix rows from the Specs, and exclusions listed?

Does `evidence/` hold only the page and the details it links to?
Does test coverage list every requirement in scope, with uncovered ones visible and covered ones backed by a passing scenario?
Do reports come from the current run, with failures and not-executed scenarios visible?
Does every test report show not-run and skipped scenarios as such, and does every scenario name the spec ids it proves?

checks.text: Is every Feature the application applies implemented once, with no second implementation (`mde verify`, Reuse row), and is every promise proven by a passing scenario tagged `@feature:<id>/<promise>` on each object that applies it (`mde verify`, Features row)?

With a database: did the last seed load rows for every entity of the Specs in the Goal's scope, as `evidence/built/seed.json` reports (`mde verify`, Seed data: every entity, not some)?

evidence.title: Build

checks.text: Is every runtime role (`mde:install`, `mde:build`, `mde:test`, `mde:start`, `mde:health`) a real script, with no successful no-op and no destructive reset inside another role (`mde verify`, Runtime scripts row)?

Does one invocation, from a fresh clone, bring up the application's own database and start all components, does health identify the application and its failing dependencies, does a second start stop the application's own previous run and start afresh, and is a port held by anything else reported and left alone?

Does `mde:start` leave its log, `evidence/tests/logs/start.log`, holding the latest start and ending with its exit, and `mde:health` its answer in `health.log`, naming the application and each dependency; did the last start succeed (`mde verify`, Start and health row)?
Does the API base come from configuration, with no hard-coded `/api` path and no fixed CORS origin in source (`mde verify`, Base path row)?
Is `build.log` present, showing `mde:build` exit 0 (`mde verify`, Build row)?
Is `test.log` present, showing the whole `mde:test` suite ran and exited 0, not a subset and not a stale run (`mde verify`, Tests row)?

evidence.title: Reuse

evidence.title: Slices and layers

evidence.title: Logging
evidence.proves: One shared logger, no console output elsewhere, and request lines carrying correlationId and principalId.

evidence.title: Live slices
evidence.proves: The API suite's captured server log shows the requests its scenarios made, each with a correlation id.

evidence.title: Stack conformance
evidence.proves: The application's dependencies are the declared stack's.

evidence.title: No placeholders
evidence.proves: No TODO, FIXME, or "not implemented" is left in shipped source.

evidence.title: Operation markers
evidence.proves: With traceability on, every entity operation is marked at its route, service, and repository.

checks.text: Is every slice live: mutations persist and the log shows the full route-to-query path (`mde verify`, Live slices row)?

Does each capability have a source folder of its own holding its slice (a route, a service, and a repository, each real code naming the capability's entities, never a placeholder), with data access (the database driver, SQL) only in the data layer and never in a route (`mde verify`, Slices and layers row)?

Is every Feature the application applies implemented once, with no second implementation (`mde verify`, Reuse row), and is every promise proven by a passing scenario tagged `@feature:<id>/<promise>` on each object that applies it (`mde verify`, Features row)?
Is each entity's model declared once, and is duplicated code below the threshold the Reuse row reports?
Is there one shared logger, with no console output elsewhere in the backend, and does it write `correlationId` and `principalId` (`mde verify`, Logging row)?
Does every implemented entity operation carry the `// MDE: <entity>.<op>` marker at its route, service, and repository (`mde verify`, Operation markers row)?
Are the declared stack's choices (backend, database, frontend, UI, build) among the application's dependencies (`mde verify`, Stack conformance row)?
Is no `TODO`, `FIXME`, or "not implemented" left in shipped source (`mde verify`, No placeholders row)?

checks.text: Is every executable check's output captured as UTF-8 under `evidence/tests/logs/`, and does each suite driving the application capture its server log, showing the requests its scenarios claim?
Do reports come from the current run, with failures and not-executed scenarios visible? Is coverage instrumented for real, with its threshold explicitly adopted and unmeasured parts named?
Is every page operation performed by a passing browser scenario (`mde verify`, Operations tested through pages: every operation, not some), and every page of the inventory used by one (Pages tested)?
Did every browser scenario leave its screenshots (`mde verify`, Screenshots: one set per scenario)?
Does every use case with a screen have a scenario walking its main flow in a browser, with screenshots after each step and at failure?
Is `evidence/tests/e2e.md` generated by the run, each step with its screenshot, and is the run instrumented for coverage?
Are behavioral scenarios readable and traced: each tagged with the spec it proves, and every entity operation with an endpoint also covered by a scenario?
Does every business rule have scenarios tagged `@rule:<id>`, where it holds and where it is refused, and every use case and entity operation a scenario (`mde verify`, Tests row)?
Does every promise of every Feature the application applies have a passing scenario tagged `@feature:<id>/<promise>` on each object that applies it (`mde verify`, Features row)?
With a database: is every entity's storage checked against the migrated database by a passing scenario (`mde verify`, Storage tested row: every entity, not some)?
Does every role-permitted operation a page renders have a UI scenario that performs it in a real browser and asserts an observable outcome, with a screenshot from the run?
Are unexecuted and blocked checks visible, never shown as passed?
Are test commands recorded and `mde:test` declared, with scoped tests run for the verification activity and the full required suite before guided release?
Does every UI scenario have a screenshot from the actual run, pass or fail, with missing captures reported?
Do reports come from the current run, with failures and not-executed scenarios visible?
Does every test report show not-run and skipped scenarios as such, and does every scenario name the spec ids it proves?
